_README.what: Unarmed combat: Punching, Wrestling and Martial Arts. PHBR1 The Complete Fighter's Handbook, book pp.74-78, with PHB pp.97-98 as the base rules PHBR1 elaborates on.
_README.replaces: THIS FILE REPLACES A FABRICATED ONE. The previous core_unarmed_martial_arts.json held 63 rows of invented content -- named styles such as Tae Kwon Do, Judo, Tai Chi Chuan, Praying Mantis, Eagle Claw, Black Tiger, Iron Body and Pressure Points, each with slot costs and damage dice, 29 of them attributed to 'Complete Fighter'. A search of all 129 pages of PHBR1 found 21 of 22 sampled names ABSENT FROM THE BOOK ENTIRELY; the one hit for 'Boxing' was an incidental use of the word. Meanwhile the maneuvers PHBR1 actually prints -- Rabbit Punch, Kidney Punch, Wild Swing, Head Punch, Elbow Shot, Vitals-Punch -- did not appear in that file at all. It was read by nothing and had sat in js/ looking authoritative for a long time.
_README.shape: PHBR1 HAS THREE STYLES AND ONE RESULTS TABLE, not a catalogue of named arts. The old file's shape was wrong as well as its content.
_README.phbDependency: THE PUNCHING AND WRESTLING RESULTS TABLE IS NOT IN PHBR1. It is PHB Table 57, p.97, and PHBR1 only refers to it -- 'Review the Punch rules from the Player's Handbook, page 98.' Its maneuvers (Wild Swing, Rabbit Punch, Kidney Punch, Glancing Blow, Jab, Uppercut, Hook, Elbow Smash, Trip, Arm Lock, Kick) are named in PHBR1's examples but never tabulated there. That table is NOT transcribed here and must come from the PHB if it is ever wanted.
_README.notOrientalAdventures: The old file marked 30 rows 'Oriental Adventures', a 1st EDITION book outside this project's 2e scope. None are carried over. PHBR1 p.76 is explicit that its Martial Arts 'aren't any real-world fighting style; they're a combination of generic martial-arts maneuvers in the tradition of martial-arts movies.'
_README.transcribedFrom: Page images of book pp.74-78. Never from OCR or memory.

styles.label: Punching
styles.baseDamage: 1-2, plus Strength bonus. A punch with a metal gauntlet does 1-3 plus Strength bonus.
styles.temporaryDamage: 75% of all punching damage is TEMPORARY and wears off within minutes after the combat is concluded.

specialization.extraAttacks: One additional punching attack per combat round. BOTH HANDS MUST BE FREE and holding nothing for the character to gain this benefit.
specialization.pullPunch: When he pulls his punch he may also refuse to do the +2 damage that specialization gives him.

styles.notes: Everyone has a certain knowledge of punching and can be considered to have a 'weapon proficiency' in it -- no slot is needed to KNOW it, only to specialize. A character can pull his punch to do no damage at all, or only his punch damage without his Strength bonus. A character using a cestus DOES add the to-hit and damage bonuses from Punching Specialization to his cestus damage; if he has specialized in the cestus too he decides round by round which set of bonuses to apply.

styles.label: Wrestling
styles.baseDamage: 1 point per successful move, plus Strength bonus if the attacker desires. A continued hold causes cumulatively 1 more point of damage each round than the round before.
styles.temporaryDamage: As with punching damage, wrestling damage is also temporary.

specialization.damage: All maneuvers do 2 points of damage plus Strength bonus, and continued holds cause cumulatively 1 more point of damage for each round they are held.
specialization.strengthForHolds: +2 to Strength, ONLY for maintaining a wrestling hold. A Strength 15 character rolls against Strength 17 when maintaining a hold, but only for that purpose.
specialization.pullDamage: When he chooses to pull wrestling damage, the character may also pull the +2 to damage granted by specialization.

styles.notes: Both characters roll normal attack rolls against the opponent's AC, using the Armor Modifiers For Wrestling table on PHB p.97. Results marked with an asterisk on PHB Table 57 mean the attacker, if successful, can maintain that hold until it is broken -- use the Strength-roll rules described for the Grab maneuver to determine when holds are broken. A character can pull wrestling damage: no damage, or the 1 point associated with each successful maneuver, or the 1 point plus Strength bonus, whichever he chooses.

styles.label: Martial Arts
styles.baseDamage: See the Martial Arts Results Table. Damage from any bare-handed Martial Arts attack is split: 25% is normal damage, the remaining 75% is temporary.
styles.temporaryDamage: 25% of the damage from the attack is normal damage; the remaining 75% is temporary.

specialization.extraAttacks: One additional Martial Arts attack per combat round. BOTH HANDS MUST BE FREE and holding nothing for the character to gain this benefit.
specialization.pullAttack: He may pull his attack just as Punching and Wrestling characters do, and when he pulls his attack he can also refuse to do the +1 damage that specialization gives him.

styles.notes: AVAILABLE ONLY IF THE DM DECIDES the art exists in the campaign. He must first decide whether he wants characters able to use these maneuvers, which will tend to give the campaign a more oriental flavor; then, if he wishes to use them, he needs to establish a history for these combat abilities -- customarily they were developed by some distant civilization, and recent trade with that culture has brought some practitioners and teachers of the art to the player-characters' society. No weapons are used. A character CAN hold a weapon in one hand and nothing in the other, attacking with his weapon one round and with his Martial Arts skill in the next. The character makes a normal attack roll against the normal Armor Class of the target -- if the ATTACKING character has armor on, he DOES suffer the Armor Modifiers For Wrestling from PHB Table 57.

martialArtsResults.source: PHBR1 p.76, Martial Arts Results Table
martialArtsResults.note: Look up the ATTACK ROLL, not the damage. A chart bonus lets the character shift his result up or down and choose any maneuver within the range his bonus covers -- a +3 bonus on a rolled 16 lets him choose anywhere from 19 down to 13. ENCODE AS A PLAIN LOOKUP, NEVER AS A FORMULA. THE TABLE IS NOT SYMMETRICAL, though it looks it at a glance. Both ends escalate away from 11/Graze, but the LOW end is deadlier at every distance: nine steps up gives Head Punch at 15% knockout, nine steps down gives High Kick at 20%, and the bottom row is Head Punch at 30%. The maneuvers do not mirror either -- 14 is an Elbow Shot where 8 is a Body-Punch, and 15 is a Side Kick where 7 is a Knee-Shot. Any implementation that generates the low half by reflecting the high half will be wrong.
martialArtsResults.damageIsTemporary: 25% normal, 75% temporary. See the style entry.

maneuvers.name: Body-Punch
maneuvers.description: A straightforward punch into the target's stomach or chest.

maneuvers.name: Elbow Shot
maneuvers.description: The attacker plants his elbow into the target's chest, side, or stomach.

maneuvers.name: Graze
maneuvers.description: This could have started out as any sort of maneuver, but it merely grazed the target; it wasn't landed firmly.

maneuvers.name: Low Kick
maneuvers.description: The attacker kicks the target in the leg or thigh.

maneuvers.name: Head Bash
maneuvers.description: The attacker slams his forehead into the target's face, which is a stout maneuver.

maneuvers.name: Head Punch
maneuvers.description: A good, strong blow with the fist to the enemy's head, particularly his jaw.

maneuvers.name: High Kick
maneuvers.description: The attacker kicks the target in the upper body somewhere: stomach, chest, back, or shoulder.

maneuvers.name: Knee-Shot
maneuvers.description: The attacker brings his knee up into the target's stomach or thigh.

maneuvers.name: Side Kick
maneuvers.description: The attacker has time to prepare and launch a very powerful sideways kick, which may be at the end of a cinematic leap.

maneuvers.name: Vitals-Kick
maneuvers.description: The attacker kicks his target at some vulnerable point: groin, kidney, neck, solar plexus, etc.

maneuvers.name: Vitals-Punch
maneuvers.description: The attacker puts his fist into one of the vulnerable points mentioned above.

rules.specializationIsNotWeaponSpecialization: Specialization in an unarmed style does NOT count as Weapon Specialization. A first-level fighter could specialize in both Long Sword and Punching if he wished. A Rogue, who cannot take any Weapon Specialization, can still take ONE unarmed fighting style specialization.
rules.fightingStylesDoNotApply: Fighting style specializations (Single-Weapon, Two-Hander and the rest) do NOT grant any bonuses to Punching, Wrestling or Martial Arts combat. They are of use only to combat with melee weapons.
rules.howManyStyles: Any character can specialize in ONE of the three unarmed styles. Only a single-class Warrior -- and the Fighting-Monk from The Complete Priest's Handbook -- may specialize in more than one.
rules.warriorProgression: A single-class Warrior can only specialize in one of the three when he is first created. After first level he may specialize in the other two, taking specialization in only one style each time he receives a new Weapon Proficiency, so he could not be a specialist in all three until sixth experience level, and ninth is more likely.
rules.usualChoice: The book's own advice: a character wanting more than one style will usually take either Martial Arts OR Punching, not both, because their usefulness overlaps a great deal, and will then take Wrestling because it is useful when the character is being grappled.

continuingSpecialization.availableTo: An option available ONLY to single-class Warriors and to Fighting-Monks from The Complete Priest's Handbook.
continuingSpecialization.restriction: The character may not take more than basic Specialization in any of the arts at FIRST experience level. At first level he may devote one slot to Punching, or one to Wrestling, or two to Martial Arts, but no more than that to any of them. At third level, when he receives another slot, he may devote it to improving his specialization.
continuingSpecialization.perSlot: For each additional slot devoted to his art: +1 to all attack rolls with that combat style, +1 to all damage with that combat style, and +1 chart bonus with all attacks in that style.
continuingSpecialization.chartBonusRange: With chart bonuses of +2 or more, the character can choose ANY maneuver within the range of maneuvers covered by his chart bonus -- not merely one row up or down.
continuingSpecialization.example: Cassius the Gladiator is a Punching Specialist. He specialized at first level, put another slot into it at third, another at sixth, and still another at ninth. At ninth level he has +3 to attack rolls, +3 to damage and a +3 chart bonus. Rolling a 16 to hit, he can choose the maneuver anywhere from 19 down to 13.

rules.orientalCampaigns: PHBR1 p.78 notes a change for oriental settings; the rule continues past the page read and is not transcribed here.
rules.fightingMonk: PHBR1 p.74 forward-references the Fighting-Monk as 'described in The Complete Priest's Handbook' -- the two books were written to interlock. PHBR3's kit gives two free weapon proficiency slots which MUST be spent on unarmed specialization, and makes the Fighting-Monk the only priest who can specialize in an unarmed combat style. See kits.js, cleric.fightingmonk.
